Oracle changes, with citations: (1) R6 norm(): FUZZ-021 r3 (89680b6b; bead.md 'Identifier validation refusals also carry an additive error object ...'): the CLI prints a refused receipt plus a CLI-only additive `error`; R6 now compares the receipt fields and separately requires that additive object to carry the refused code and details. The run-3 norm dropped operation/schema whenever `error` was present, which made 4/seed false mismatches (dash-step was one; it passes under the new norm). The first R6 pass (4 fails/seed) is kept in first-pass/ and not counted; R6 was re-run on fresh ws-d4ci/ws-d4di. The 3 remaining R6 failures per seed are a real CLI-vs-Python divergence (differential-n01), not an oracle artefact: ADR-0023 says GraphIdInvalid is 'a receipt (Rust Ok, Python receipt, CLI exit 2)'. (2) K: the first K pass used colliding case names for the new registry FUZZ-013 cases; it was renamed (FUZZ-013-registry-*) and re-run on a fresh ws-d4az; the first pass (29/30, same single failure) is in first-pass/ and not counted. (3) R4fake 1-rename-pour: the run-2/run-3 harness oracle (expects GRAPH_APPLY_FAILED for pour too) is kept unchanged and still counted failed, attributed to FUZZ-047 (intentional boundary: ADR-0023 pour ids are bd-assigned). The new K case FUZZ-047-rename-pour-bd-assigned judges the same behaviour against the ADR-0023 contract and passes. No contract in the brief's list required changing an R1-R4, R7-R9 oracle: FUZZ-012 r3 (relative rendered_formula) is not used by these families (absolute paths); FUZZ-015 r3 batching not exercised beyond K's 40-step case; FUZZ-040/054 recovery escaping exercised by R6c/R9 token comparison (pass). data.notes: Harness: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-randlee-github-sc-compose/ad60cb14-c875-41a7-825f-3b1e466350d8/scratchpad/campaign4/workers/differential-probe/lib (run-3 scripts copied from campaign3/workers/differential-probe/lib; fam.sh retargeted to campaign4/env.sh (Dolt 53058), agg.py campaign path, bd prefixes d4*; no script contained a dfdf4aa label or port literal). Fresh bd workspaces ws-d4<xx> created by mkws (no mkws timeout or retry needed). Same case counts as run 3: r1 14/8, r2 12/7, r3 9/6, r4 14/8, r4fake 10/10, r5 74+r5c 16 per seed, r6 33, r6b 4, r6c 5/3 cases (66/52 results), r6cap 24, r7 3x5/2x5 + r7s 2x4 shared + r7c 3x4/2x4, r7append 10 trials per seed, r8 8/6, r9 6/4. Family K is seed-independent (run under seed 7023 as in run 3; each case 3 reps, passes only if all 3 pass) and was extended from 9 to 30 cases: FUZZ-013 residual (registry validate/preview-pour/pour of 'a..b','re g0','café' head vs baseline, and formula_name '' on preview-pour/pour -> BEADS_FORMULA_NAME_REQUIRED), FUZZ-051 (4 append templates), FUZZ-055 (registry preview-pour/pour argv, attach create --graph argv, cook-failure diagnostic, JSON and human), FUZZ-047 (fake-bd rename on pour and attach under the ADR-0023 oracle). FUZZ-022, FUZZ-027, FUZZ-045 have no documented oracle and were re-checked 3x as uncounted observations (k-observations-7023.json). Oracle changes, with citations: (1) R6 norm(): FUZZ-021 r3 (89680b6b; bead.md 'Identifier validation refusals also carry an additive error object ...'): the CLI prints a refused receipt plus a CLI-only additive `error`; R6 now compares the receipt fields and separately requires that additive object to carry the refused code and details. The run-3 norm dropped operation/schema whenever `error` was present, which made 4/seed false mismatches (dash-step was one; it passes under the new norm). The first R6 pass (4 fails/seed) is kept in first-pass/ and not counted; R6 was re-run on fresh ws-d4ci/ws-d4di. The 3 remaining R6 failures per seed are a real CLI-vs-Python divergence (differential-n01), not an oracle artefact: ADR-0023 says GraphIdInvalid is 'a receipt (Rust Ok, Python receipt, CLI exit 2)'. (2) K: the first K pass used colliding case names for the new registry FUZZ-013 cases; it was renamed (FUZZ-013-registry-*) and re-run on a fresh ws-d4az; the first pass (29/30, same single failure) is in first-pass/ and not counted. (3) R4fake 1-rename-pour: the run-2/run-3 harness oracle (expects GRAPH_APPLY_FAILED for pour too) is kept unchanged and still counted failed, attributed to FUZZ-047 (intentional boundary: ADR-0023 pour ids are bd-assigned). The new K case FUZZ-047-rename-pour-bd-assigned judges the same behaviour against the ADR-0023 contract and passes. No contract in the brief's list required changing an R1-R4, R7-R9 oracle: FUZZ-012 r3 (relative rendered_formula) is not used by these families (absolute paths); FUZZ-015 r3 batching not exercised beyond K's 40-step case; FUZZ-040/054 recovery escaping exercised by R6c/R9 token comparison (pass). Every family ran; none was skipped.

findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 (Codes): 'A BeadId, GraphRef or StepId that fails its newtype rule instead returns GraphIdInvalid (refused / exit 2, with field, value and rule)' and 'Everything in the table is a receipt (Rust Ok, Python receipt, CLI exit 2)'; request errors raised as Python exceptions are only request-shape problems. bead.md 'Identifier validation refusals ...' (89680b6b). R6 oracle: CLI receipt == Python receipt

Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator, head vs baseline.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Decision 1 and Consequences; ADR-0021 FormulaNameRequired
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: either keep the grammar and amend ADR-0021/0023 (documenting the breaking change), or confine the grammar to the uses that need it (registry path, graph metadata).
findings.root_cause: Commit e1b5168 made BeadComposeRequest.formula_name a validating FormulaName newtype, so serde rejects names outside [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* during request parsing.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate formula_name only where it becomes a path or bd argument, with a stable code, and keep Phase R parsing unchanged; or record the break in an ADR.

findings.command: two concurrent `sc-compose bead attach` requests with the same parent and rendered_formula, different ref and compose_variables.tag
findings.minimal_template: formula = "x" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / [[steps]] id = "a" title = "A {{{ tag }}}"
findings.minimal_input: request k: ref race<k>, compose_variables {"tag":"T<k>"}, rendered_formula <ws>/build/x.formula.toml
findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Atomic apply and Revision: each request's beads come from its own rendered text; GraphApplyFailed means bd wrote nothing.
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0001 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): Coordinator repro (3 trials): trial 1: a failed receipt (GraphApplyFailed, 'nothing was written') whose own bd create returned ids for the other request's plan; trial 2: a succeeded receipt for ref race20 created a bead titled 'A T21', i.e. the other request's content. Worker saw cross-contamination in 27/27 trials. Deterministic regression via a path-honest fake bd.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Decision 6, Graph plan, Revision, Errors (GraphApplyFailed); UC-9
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed for the invariant; if a shared rendered_formula is to be unsupported, document and refuse it.
findings.root_cause: graph::run re-reads rendered_formula from disk and bd cooks it by path, and PendingCreate::execute writes then applies the fixed path <rendered_formula>.graph.json, so concurrent requests sharing the path race on both files.
findings.recommended_fix: Hash and cook the bytes this request rendered (private copy), and write the plan to a per-invocation path or hold a lock across render-cook-apply.

findings.minimal_input: attach request with "parent":"--help" (or "--version"); or relation {"from":"step:a","to":"bead:--db=/nonexistent","type":"related"}
findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Conflict rules / Relation validation: a missing parent is BEADS_GRAPH_PARENT_NOT_FOUND and a missing bead: endpoint is GraphRelationInvalid(bead_not_found). BeadId only requires non-empty, no whitespace.
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0001 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): Exit 2 failed BEADS_GRAPH_READ_FAILED; argv ['bd','show','--help','--help.inj-a',...] and ['bd','show','--db=/nonexistent',...]: bd parsed the ids as options and, for --db=, opened a different database. Controls with ordinary missing ids give the documented codes. Reproduced 3/3 per variant by the coordinator. No write is reachable.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Conflict rules, Relation validation; BeadId contract
findings.root_cause: Request ids are spliced into `bd show <ids...> --json` and `bd dep list <id> --json` with no `--` separator.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass ids after `--` (bd v1.3.1 accepts it) or reject bead ids starting with '-' at the BeadId boundary.

findings.minimal_input: no variables; destination absent
findings.expected_oracle: help render 'Appending JSON records' step 2: the object is parsed and re-serialized and only its key order may differ; FR-7 render --append.
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0001 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): Exit 0; appended {"amount":0.1,"id":1.2345678901234568e+22}. Integers above u64 become lossy floats, long decimals round, 1e2 -> 100.0, -0 -> -0.0. Plain render passes the body unchanged. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator; --append does not exist on origin/develop.
findings.requirement_trace: FR-7 render --append; FR-8a; help render 'Appending JSON records'
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed; if normalization is intended, the manual must say so.
findings.root_cause: append_json_record parses into serde_json::Value without arbitrary_precision and re-serializes.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate the object but keep the original number tokens (arbitrary_precision or RawValue plus minification).

findings.subsystem: graph pour confinement order
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0001 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): A graph-mode preview-pour with rendered_formula outside working_directory writes the file and runs bd cook --dry-run before refusing with BEADS_OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR at resolve_active_registry; this follows the Phase R registry exception (mode known only after bd where). The refusal code differs from baseline (BEADS_FORMULA_OUTSIDE_ACTIVE_REGISTRY).
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0021 lines 207-215 (Paths): 'All paths resolve relative to working_directory ... PreviewPour and Pour are the deliberate exception because their output must be in the active Beads registry resolved by bd where.'; ADR-0023 line 350: 'A rendered formula outside working_directory is refused as before.'; ADR-0021 line 172: 'OutputOutsideWorkingDirectory | BEADS_OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR | Rendered output escapes the permitted working directory.'
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new doc needed; optional follow-up to refuse before writing.
adr_citations: ADR-0021 lines 207-215 (Paths): 'All paths resolve relative to working_directory ... PreviewPour and Pour are the deliberate exception because their output must be in the active Beads registry resolved by bd where.' -- authorises rendering before the registry/mode is known, so the file is written before the refusal (unchanged from baseline 080f261).
ADR-0023 line 350: 'A rendered formula outside working_directory is refused as before.' -- authorises the refusal under the graph-pour mode selection.

ADR-0021 line 172: 'OutputOutsideWorkingDirectory | BEADS_OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR | Rendered output escapes the permitted working directory.' -- the code now emitted (pour.rs refuse_outside_workspace, commit 6a5116c) is the variant whose documented meaning is exactly this condition.
findings.note: The ADRs do not name which code the outside-workdir pour refusal uses; baseline used FORMULA_OUTSIDE_ACTIVE_REGISTRY (ADR-0021 line 185), head uses OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR. Exit 2 and stage are unchanged. Recommend a one-line ADR-0023/manual clarification naming the code (doc follow-up, not a code defect). Reproduced 3/3 head vs baseline (r5-mm-06, 8 cases).
findings.tested_head_evidence: boundary-probe: still_reproduces; fuzz024_031 024:head:preview_pour/pour r0-r2: exit 2 BEADS_OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR at resolve_active_registry after cook <outside>/z.formula.toml + where; outside_files ['z.formula.toml']; bd unchanged. paths *:rendered_outside_graph same. Ruled intentional_boundary in run 2 | differential-probe: still_reproduces; r5-mm-06 (8 cases): e.g. 7023:outside-workdir-ow0:preview-pour head exit 2 BEADS_OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR at resolve_active_registry after render+validate; rendered file left on disk (baseline too). Intentional boundary

findings.command: sc-compose bead attach --request $'\xff' --json   (also bead render --request $'req\xff.json' without --json)
findings.minimal_template: n/a
findings.minimal_input: request path argv containing one non-UTF-8 byte (0xFF), file absent
findings.expected_oracle: help bead: request-file read failures use BEADS_REQUEST_READ_FAILED (exit 3) with details.path/kind and recovery; FR-7 stable envelope, never a panic. Baseline 080f261: exit 3 envelope.
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0002 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): Exit 101, empty stdout: thread 'main' panicked at crates/sc-composer-beads/src/error_json.rs:25:17: called Result::unwrap() on Err 'path contains invalid UTF-8 characters'. JSON and human mode. Coordinator 3/3; baseline exit 3.
findings.requirement_trace: help bead Request-file read failures; ADR-0023 Request errors; FR-7
findings.root_cause: impl Serialize for BeadComposeError builds json!({"path": path, ...}) for RequestReadFailed; json! unwraps serde_json::to_value(PathBuf), which fails for non-UTF-8 paths. Reached via print_json and human_bead_error.
findings.recommended_fix: Serialize the path lossily (to_string_lossy) or as bytes and never unwrap in the error serializer.
findings.tested_head_evidence: boundary-probe: not_re_exercised; non-UTF-8 directory cases cannot be created on APFS (Errno 92) | shape-probe: fixed; f8-045/f8-046 both seeds and 3x: --request $'<cases>/req\xff.json' gives exit 3 BEADS_REQUEST_READ_FAILED with details.path lossy (U+FFFD), in JSON and human mode. Output path (050df6f4): the library probe f38probe with rendered_formula <wd>/missing-\xff/o.formula.toml serialized 3/3 to BEADS_OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID with details.value lossy, no serializer error. The CLI and Python cannot reach this path because requests carry UTF-8 strings.

findings.command: sc-compose bead preview-attach --request f10-dollar-subshell-preview-attach.json | grep '^bd dep add' | sh
findings.minimal_template: formula u: step 'head', step 'tail' needs ['head']
findings.minimal_input: existing parent with bd-accepted id 'spc-$(id)58' (also 'spc-a;b90', 'spc-x"q65', ESC/bidi/C0 ids); attach, bd dep remove tail head, re-run
findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Errors: GraphEdgeMissing recovery is 'run the bd dep add command the message gives'; the message lists 'the exact command'. help bead: each recovery command printed on its own line.
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0002 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): Printed 'bd dep add spc-$(id)58.rdollar_subshellv2-tail spc-$(id)58.rdollar_subshellv2-head --type blocks' unquoted: a shell runs `id`; ';' splits the command; quotes merge args; control/bidi characters reach the terminal raw. Receipt missing_edges data itself is correct. Coordinator 3/3.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Errors (GraphEdgeMissing); help bead human output
findings.root_cause: Commands built with plain Display format!("bd dep add {} {} --type {}") with no shell quoting or control escaping; BeadId only forbids whitespace.
findings.recommended_fix: Shell-quote each argument (and escape control characters) in the human and message forms, or reject such ids at BeadId.
findings.tested_head_evidence: boundary-probe: fixed; missing_edges 22/22 in ws/e: quoted recovery commands shell-parse to the exact argv in plan order and run_human_cmd x5 succeed | differential-probe: fixed; R6c (66/66, 52/52) and R9 (36/36, 24/24): human and JSON 'bd dep add' recovery commands are token-equal to missing_edges and running them repaired the edge | shape-probe: fixed; f10 160/160 (7023) and 96/96 (48611). The run-3 failing cases (7023 f10-084/087/116/119 rlo/zwsp; 48611 f10-028/031/044/047) pass: e.g. rlo prints bd dep add $'s4c-\xE2\x80\xAEx81.rrlov2-tail' ... with no raw RLO/ZWSP, and sh/bash/zsh give the exact argv. End to end 3x: printed line run by bash with real bd restores the edges and the re-run is a no-op. | template-probe: not_re_exercised; Injection repro not run by this worker. Incidentally: D2/R bd dep add recovery lines are shell-quoted and execute correctly via shlex.split (60/60 D2, R edge_missing)

findings.subsystem: render --append record serialization (nested whitespace)
findings.command: printf '{"a":[1,\n2]}' > nl.json.j2; sc-compose render --file nl.json.j2 --root . --append nl.jsonl
findings.minimal_input: destination absent
findings.expected_oracle: render.md 'Appending JSON records' step 3: 'writes it as one compact UTF-8 line (embedded newlines stay escaped) followed by \n'.
findings.observed_result: Historical observation from t7-20261007-0003 (preserved definition, not run4 behavior): Exit 0; nl.jsonl holds 2 physical lines '{"a":[1,' and '2]}', neither valid JSON. Nested whitespace is kept ({"z":[1, 2]}); only the top level is compacted. The concurrent-append family did not hit this because its records keep nested values on one line.
findings.requirement_trace: render.md steps 2-3; FR-7 render --append (JSON Lines)
findings.root_cause: append_json_record re-serializes a BTreeMap<String, Box<RawValue>>, so each top-level value's raw text (including newlines and spaces) is written verbatim.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-serialize nested values compactly while preserving number lexemes (e.g. serde_json arbitrary_precision Value), or minify RawValue text outside strings.

finding.minimal_template: wf/rel.formula.toml.j2 (build; verify needs build; publish needs verify)
finding.minimal_input: preview_attach request, parent b4a-x29 (exists), ref m1, relations [{from step:build, to bead:x, type related}] where 'x' is a substring of the parent id and no bead 'x' exists
finding.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Conflict rules L462-468: 'A bead is absent only on bd's not-found response: the id is missing from a list that bd show returned with exit 0' -> the endpoint is absent -> BEADS_GRAPH_RELATION_INVALID 'invalid graph relation 0: bead_not_found' (as for the control bead:zqzq, 3/3)
finding.observed: exit 2 BEADS_GRAPH_READ_FAILED: 'graph read failed (Some(0)): bd show returned an unexpected or duplicate issue id; [bd show --json -- b4a-x29 ... x]; fix bd and retry, nothing was written' (3/3). bd's partial-id matching resolves 'x' to b4a-x29, so the row set contains the parent twice. Fails safe (nothing written) but the code and recovery blame bd for a user endpoint that does not exist. Data-dependent: it reproduces whenever an endpoint id is a partial match of a requested or other bead id (an unrequested match gives the same 'unexpected' error)
finding.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Conflict rules (bead absent only on bd not-found); bead.md L159-162 and code table L384
finding.owning_file: crates/sc-composer-beads/src/graph.rs GraphReader::issues (~L313-319: unexpected/duplicate row id -> read_error; present since a55cef11, batching 4f13497b)

finding.minimal_input: preview_attach request with parent 'a b' (or ''), valid ref
finding.expected_oracle: bead.md L323-325: error.details carries `field`, rejected `value` and `rule`; run-4 oracle assumed field names the request field ('parent'), as it does for ref ('ref')
finding.observed: exit 2 refused receipt (correct) with details {field 'bead', value 'a b', rule 'bead ids are non-empty without whitespace'} (3/3); an invalid relation endpoint bead:'a b' gives the identical error (xmin4 endpoint_bad 3/3), so a consumer cannot tell the parent from an endpoint. tpl/nzero.formula.toml.j2: formula = "nzero" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / [[steps]] id = "a" title = "A"

Expected
ADR-0023 (Codes): 'A BeadId, GraphRef or StepId that fails its newtype rule instead returns GraphIdInvalid (refused / exit 2, with field, value and rule)' and 'Everything in the table is a receipt (Rust Ok, Python receipt, CLI exit 2)'; request errors raised as Python exceptions are only request-shape problems. bead.md 'Identifier validation refusals ...' (89680b6b). R6 oracle: CLI receipt == Python receipt
Observed
CLI (3/3): exit 2, refused receipt {outcome:{refused:{code:BEADS_GRAPH_ID_INVALID}}, stages:[validate failed BEADS_GRAPH_ID_INVALID 'invalid graph ref `a.b`; follow ADR-0023: ref is [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}']} plus additive error {code, details{field:'ref',rule,value:'a.b'}, recovery}. Python (3/3): the BeadComposeRequest constructor raises BeadComposeError(code='BEADS_GRAPH_ID_INVALID', stage='validate', details={'field':'ref','value':'a.b'}) - an exception, no receipt, and details lack the 'rule'. Minimal template / frontmatter

FUZZ-055 contract (f5277c41, 8a0ead8d): receipts/argv/diagnostics present the rendered_formula / public source path, not the deleted .sc-compose-input-* snapshot; FR-8 diagnostics name a file the user can act on. The published plan is <rendered_formula>.graph.json (d2c5704d publishes it before bd create --graph).
Observed
rc 2 failed BEADS_GRAPH_APPLY_FAILED (correct, bd's cycle cause carried), but the apply stage argv is ['bd','create','--graph','<ws>/build/.sc-compose-input-98316-1791416388740305000-1.json','--dry-run','--json'], stderr_excerpt and human stage line repeat that path, error details.command repeats it, and the validate stage stdout_excerpt (bd cook JSON 'source') names '<ws>/build/.sc-compose-input-<pid>-<ts>-0.formula.toml'. Root cause
Observed ownership: crates/sc-composer-beads/src/graph.rs: execute() lines 92-101 map only formula_input (the formula snapshot) back to rendered_formula and only in argv/stderr_excerpt (not stdout_excerpt, not the error details); the plan snapshot created at lines 401-408 (InputSnapshot::write + publish_copy, argv uses plan_input.path()) is never mapped back to the published <rendered_formula>.graph.json. Already addressed above the tested head by comp-t-7.33 / #737; this campaign did not retest that fix.
